mhac_question: Rank auditory icons, earcons, spearcons and speech on identification accuracy, response time, preference, workload and dual-task cost (RQ3)
comparator_evidence: C1 does exactly this with searches to mid-2021, k = 11–50 per outcome and an NMA ranking
consequence_for_scope: MHAC will not produce another cue-family ranking. Any such comparison is an explicitly labelled update or sensitivity check against C1, never a novelty claim.
revision_trigger: VoR shows materially different scope; or a later review already updates C1

mhac_question: Separate recognition/identification from correct task action within a deadline (RQ3, RQ6)
comparator_evidence: C1 codes accuracy as % correct and describes tasks descriptively; no action-versus-identification distinction found. C2 summary says research has focused on how messages are delivered rather than their content (rail-crossing domain).
consequence_for_scope: Retained as an evidence-map axis and estimand family (O1 vs O2). Value claimed only if primary studies with action outcomes exist and the separation changes conclusions.
revision_trigger: A review or standard already separating identification from action is found in R004/R005

mhac_question: Training dose, learning burden and delayed retention as distinct outcomes (RQ3)
comparator_evidence: C1 did not code training, practice or retention (tool-mediated reading). Pilot found primary learnability/retention reports (titles only).
consequence_for_scope: Retained as outcome families O4/O5 with explicit dose and delay windows.
revision_trigger: A review of auditory-cue learning/retention is located

mhac_question: Perceived urgency and its mapping to hazard, severity and time-to-action (RQ3, RQ4)
comparator_evidence: C1 excluded urgency ratings as polarity-ambiguous. A substantial urgency-mapping literature exists (C10, unread). Updated in R004: C12's abstracts show perceived urgency predicted from acoustic parameters and scaled psychophysically. C11 maps event criticality (low, medium, high) to informing, warning, alarming and urging sounds, and to compliance levels with response-time bands (none; 15–30 min; 1–5 min; 5–30 s) for ICU alarms (PDF p. 14).
consequence_for_scope: MHAC must not claim novelty for mapping urgency to hazard and time-to-action: C11 already chains them in one domain. Any MHAC contribution is limited to what C11 and the urgency-mapping tradition lack, and that must be shown by reading them in full. Urgency is analysed as mapping fidelity, not "higher is better".
revision_trigger: Urgency-mapping reviews and alarm standards read; C11 read in full; overlap re-judged

comparator_evidence: C5 tests audiovisual mappings for probability (loudness, pitch, tempo with visual channels; N = 170/185 crowd-sourced) without alerts, urgency or action; reports that preferred pairings are not necessarily good probability mappings. "Sounds Uncertain" (arXiv 2608.18680) is affect-focused but unread.
consequence_for_scope: Uncertainty sonification is an existing line; MHAC's possible contribution is only its integration with urgency, hazard and requested action in alerts.
revision_trigger: Evidence that integrated uncertainty-plus-action alerts were already studied

mhac_question: Keep source, certainty, hazard, consequence, urgency, persistence and action distinct in one model (RQ4)
comparator_evidence: No inspected comparator integrates these dimensions. Pieces exist: urgency mapping (C10), uncertainty mapping (C5), delivery/content distinction (C2). Updated in R004: C11 integrates event criticality, alarm informativeness (urgency, detectability, localisability, masking, learnability) and required action in one framework (PDF pp. 13–14). A whole-text term search found no message-certainty dimension. Lifecycle problems (alarms still sounding after recovery) appear only in interview quotations (PDF p. 11), not as a framework dimension.
consequence_for_scope: The candidate integrative contribution narrows to certainty and persistence/lifecycle together with the dimensions C11 already combines. It remains conditional on the remove-Brier test and on no alarm standard already encoding them.
revision_trigger: A human-factors alarm taxonomy or standard already encoding these dimensions

mhac_question: Retaining functions without performed human emotion; distinguishing prosody, human likeness, attributed emotion and listener affect (RQ5)
comparator_evidence: C1 does not address human likeness or affect. Pilot queries surfaced HRI voice/trust and synthetic-emotion work (titles only). Updated in R004: C13: Kühne et al. report humanlike voices rated less eerie and more likable, contrary to an uncanny-valley expectation (PDF p. 1). Becker et al. report a natural robot voice perceived as safer and increasing reliance on repeated incorrect advice, without a direct trust effect. Romeo et al. report more behavioural trust in a state-of-the-art synthetic voice although questionnaires indicated the opposite (abstracts). C14 surveys agent voice and argues for aligned rather than maximally human-like voices (abstracts). None of the material read separates prosody, human likeness, attributed emotion and listener affect.
consequence_for_scope: No contribution is claimed on whether human-like voices help or harm. Contrary evidence exists and goes to #6 for Track E screening. Any MHAC contribution is limited to the four-way distinction, if full reading shows that the comparators lack it.
revision_trigger: Full reading of C13 and C14, or a review of voice anthropomorphism or emotion in alerts

mhac_question: Peircean sign-type classification of interface sounds (icon/index/symbol)
comparator_evidence: C4 already classifies verbal messages, earcons and auditory icons with Peircean sign classes and links interpretation effort to communicability. Its classes differ from the project's earlier informal assignments. Updated in R004: two further semiotic treatments of interface sound were identified (C15) but not read: Oswald (2012) is unavailable and Murphy et al. (2006) is metadata only. Parmentier (2009) questions the utility of Peirce's trichotomies for social analysis (title only).
consequence_for_scope: MHAC cannot present Peircean classification of alert sounds as new. Sign relations are treated as relation-dependent hypotheses (glossary G14).
revision_trigger: Full C4 reading; Oswald (2012) obtained; or further semiotics-of-sound literature

mhac_question: Communication-centred evaluation of interfaces via designer-to-user messages (RQ6)
comparator_evidence: C6 semiotic engineering provides metacommunication and communicability evaluation and has been applied to aural/tactile mobile interfaces (2009 abstract). Updated in R004: the founding article (de Souza 1993), the communicability evaluation method (Prates et al. 2000) and the methods book (de Souza and Leitão 2009) were identified (C16, metadata only). No open copy of the core chapters was located.
consequence_for_scope: Strong redundancy risk: any MHAC evaluation contract must state what it adds beyond semiotic engineering. R004/R008 must read de Souza's core chapters.
revision_trigger: Close reading shows semiotic engineering lacks or already supplies the RQ4 distinctions

mhac_question: Apply cybersemiotics to machine–human audio communication (RQ1–RQ6)
comparator_evidence: Inspected Brier texts (C7) do not address HCI, interfaces or sound; they mention robots/machines only in passing. C8 applies cybersemiotics to discourse pragmatics; C9 critiques its constructivism. Updated in R003: Jacques (2021), chapter 10 of the Vidales and Brier volume, applies Brier's framework to user-interface design and interactive environments; its abstract and visible notes show no sound, alerts or user evaluation (abstract only, SRC-BRIER-REC-JACQUES-2021-CH10).
consequence_for_scope: A cybersemiotic HCI application already exists, so MHAC cannot claim to be the first; an audio-message application was still not found. Only the remove-Brier test (R011) can show whether anything substantive changes.
revision_trigger: Reading Jacques (2021) in full; any located cybersemiotic audio work; or the subtraction test showing no change

comparator_evidence: Brier's own expositions (C7) and an edited introductory volume exist; reception includes Cobley (C9).
consequence_for_scope: Reconstruction is a dependency for the applied question, not a claimed contribution. Value lies in locator-bound fidelity and critique.

mhac_question: Comparison of cybersemiotics with alternatives and a subtraction test (RQ2)
comparator_evidence: No inspected source compares cybersemiotics with human-factors or semiotic-engineering accounts for interface communication. Updated in R004: fourteen negative-case searches across eleven clusters found no such comparison.
consequence_for_scope: Retained as the decisive applied test; outcome may be that the contribution is organisational only or redundant.
revision_trigger: R004 reception search finds such a comparison

mhac_question: Update of the brief-alert evidence after C1's 2021 search
comparator_evidence: C1 searched April–June 2021. Pilot surfaced at least one later relevant report (2022 working-memory study).
consequence_for_scope: A dated update window (2021-04-01 to 2026-10-04) is a legitimate, modest aim, reported as an update rather than novelty.
